title: 2 Chronicles 21
paragraphs: ¹ Jehoshaphat rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the city of David. Then his son Jehoram became king in his place. ² He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel. ³ Their father had given them generous gifts of silver, gold, and precious goods, along with fortified cities in Judah — but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn. ⁴ When Jehoram had established himself over his father's kingdom, he put all his brothers to the sword, along with some of the princes of Israel. ⁵ Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

⁶ He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he had married Ahab's daughter. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. ⁷ Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant he had made with David, and because he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his descendants forever. ⁸ In his days Edom revolted against Judah's rule and set up its own king. ⁹ So Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots. He rose by night and broke through the Edomites who had surrounded him, along with the chariot commanders. ¹⁰ Yet Edom has been in revolt against Judah's rule ever since. Libnah also revolted at the same time from under his authority, because he had forsaken the LORD, the God of his ancestors.

¹¹ Furthermore, he built high places on the hillsides of Judah, led the inhabitants of Jerusalem into spiritual adultery, and dragged Judah along with them. ¹² Then a letter reached him from Elijah the prophet, saying: "This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or in the ways of Asa king of Judah, ¹³ but have walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and have led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem into the same unfaithfulness as the house of Ahab, and because you have also murdered your own brothers, your father's family, men who were better than you — ¹⁴ the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives, and all your possessions with a heavy blow. ¹⁵ You yourself will suffer a severe illness, a disease of the bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day after day."

¹⁶ Moreover, the LORD stirred up against Jehoram the hostility of the Philistines and of the Arabians who border the Ethiopians. ¹⁷ They attacked Judah, invaded it, and carried off all the property they found in the king's palace, along with his sons and wives. Not a son was left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest. ¹⁸ And after all this, the LORD struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease. ¹⁹ In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in great agony. His people did not make a fire in his honor as they had done for his ancestors. ²⁰ He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He passed away to no one's regret, and they buried him in the city of David — but not in the tombs of the kings.
